reason: Once the chants were recognised, the first reading's syllables were reread against the chant texts. This placed the strip, joined piece 4v to strip 2r and showed that the John antiphon is the 6 May one.
sources: Klosterneuburg, Stiftsbibliothek, CCl 1018, ff. 36v-38r, Cantus Database inventory (source 123616)

text:
Source-assisted reading of F-17j8 (Stams, Frg. 257). Reread on the native images at reading size, with Cantus Index texts at hand: every text line of strip 2r (canvas 2), pieces 3r, 4r, 6r (canvas 2) and 4v (canvas 3), strip 2v (canvas 3, also reread by a second research reader), and a mirrored, contrast-stretched crop of the set-off on the board (canvas 0). Pieces 3v, 5r, 5v, 6v, 7r, 7v rest on the first reading. Boxes are x,y,width,height in native pixels; y values are approximate line centres. (x) expansion, [ ] lost or supplied, ? doubtful.
